observation.visible_scene: An overcast mountain panorama: layered dark forested ridges recede into the distance, with bare dead-tree branches silhouetted in the lower foreground. A thick sea of white fog/cloud fills the valleys below the ridgelines, and a heavy gray cloud deck covers the sky. The composition is essentially a wide landscape shot with no people or animals.
visible_changes: The valley fog sea drifts and morphs very slowly and continuously across the excerpt: its billowy surface texture reshapes and the bright fog bands hugging the left and central ridges shift slightly relative to the static mountains.
The overhead cloud layer in the sky also creeps and re-textures gradually, with subtle changes in the brightness and shape of cloud patches from frame 1 to frame 41.

The mountains, ridgelines and foreground branches remain fixed in position relative to the frame edges, indicating the camera is essentially stationary (no evident pan, tilt or zoom) and the only motion is atmospheric.
No object enters, exits, or occludes another; the fog never fully covers a ridge nor clears away within the segment—the changes are small-scale drifts of an already-present, ongoing flow.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the fog is rising, sinking or flowing laterally as a coherent mass cannot be resolved from this short excerpt; the motion may have begun before t=0 and continues after t=2.67s.
Any wind conditions, time of day, or season beyond what the gray light suggests are not determinable.
uncertain_details: A possible extremely slow camera drift cannot be fully excluded, but the consistent alignment of ridges and branches argues against significant camera motion.
The exact direction and speed of the fog/cloud movement are subtle and hard to pin down frame-to-frame.
